intro: Three free pieces I think are worth your time this week, chosen from the Substacks I follow most closely. Each one opens on the writer's own Substack.

items.title: My Visit to Alpha School (a three-part series)
items.why: I've been following the Alpha School story with great interest, and this is the most thorough first-hand account I've read. Wexler visits the Austin campus, hears from Carl Hendrick on why technology may be the way to deliver well-sequenced, systematic instruction at scale, and weighs up the concerns too. Parts 2 and 3 are on her Substack.

items.title: No Notes: Why I’d ban "copying from the board"
items.why: Adam Boxer makes a persuasive case that students copying notes from the board learn very little. He suggests handing out the notes and spending that time on questioning and practice instead, which would make a great conversation starter with your team before planning for next year.

items.title: Observing the unobservable
items.why: Australian teacher Shaun Brien on why peer observation so often misses what expert teachers actually do. His practical suggestions, like agreeing on a focus before the lesson and tracking the rate and type of questions, are worth a look as you plan observations for next year.
